title: Bug: create_react_agent doesn't actually take in a ToolExecutor
body:
### Checked other resources

- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I searched the [LangGraph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/)/LangChain documentation with the integrated search.
- [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [X] I am sure that this is a bug in LangGraph/LangChain rather than my code.
- [X] I am sure this is better as an issue [rather than a GitHub discussion](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/discussions/new/choose), since this is a LangGraph bug and not a design question.

### Example Code

```python
from typing import Literal

from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langgraph.prebuilt.tool_executor import ToolExecutor
from langchain_core.tools import tool
from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent

openai_api_key = "sk-..."

model = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o", temperature=0, api_key=openai_api_key)


@tool
def get_weather(city: Literal["nyc", "sf"]):
    """Use this to get weather information."""
    if city == "nyc":
        return "It might be cloudy in nyc"
    elif city == "sf":
        return "It's always sunny in sf"
    else:
        raise AssertionError("Unknown city")


# this works fine
tools = [get_weather]
# this does not
tools = ToolExecutor([get_weather])


# Define the graph


graph = create_react_agent(
    model,
    tools=tools,
)


def print_stream(stream):
    for s in stream:
        message = s["messages"][-1]
        if isinstance(message, tuple):
            print(message)
        else:
            message.pretty_print()


message = "What is the weather in SF and new york?"


inputs = {
    "messages": [
        ("user", message),
    ]
}
print_stream(graph.stream(inputs, stream_mode="values"))
```


### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell
graph = create_react_agent(
            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/conda/envs/sevin/lib/python3.12/site-packages/langgraph/_api/deprecation.py", line 54, in wrapper
    return func(*args, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/conda/envs/sevin/lib/python3.12/site-packages/langgraph/prebuilt/chat_agent_executor.py", line 611, in create_react_agent
    workflow.add_node("tools", ToolNode(tools))
                               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/conda/envs/sevin/lib/python3.12/site-packages/langgraph/prebuilt/tool_node.py", line 79, in __init__
    for tool_ in tools:
TypeError: 'ToolExecutor' object is not iterable
```


### Description

In the type hints for create_react_agent, it says that tools can be passed in as a ToolExecutor, but in practice this does not work.


### System Info

langchain==0.2.1
langchain-anthropic==0.1.16
langchain-community==0.2.1
langchain-core==0.2.23
langchain-elasticsearch==0.2.1
langchain-mistralai==0.1.8
langchain-openai==0.1.8
langchain-text-splitters==0.2.0
langchainhub==0.1.17

linked_prs.title: fix: the execution error passed from ToolExecutor to create_react_agent
linked_prs.patch:
diff --git a/libs/langgraph/langgraph/prebuilt/chat_agent_executor.py b/libs/langgraph/langgraph/prebuilt/chat_agent_executor.py
index 86a1c13e58d..546ad53bc26 100644
--- a/libs/langgraph/langgraph/prebuilt/chat_agent_executor.py
+++ b/libs/langgraph/langgraph/prebuilt/chat_agent_executor.py
@@ -474,7 +474,7 @@ async def acall_model(state: AgentState, config: RunnableConfig):
 
     # Define the two nodes we will cycle between
     workflow.add_node("agent", RunnableLambda(call_model, acall_model))
-    workflow.add_node("tools", ToolNode(tools))
+    workflow.add_node("tools", ToolNode(tool_classes))
 
     # Set the entrypoint as `agent`
     # This means that this node is the first one called
